messages.text: What is the bright object in the eastern sky? Looking from my address in Glendale AZ.

As of 3:37 PM on January 9, 2025, in Glendale, Arizona, the bright object you observe in the eastern sky is likely the planet Jupiter. Jupiter is prominently visible from early evening through pre-dawn hours in January, with its brightness gradually decreasing each day. It rises and sets approximately four minutes earlier each day; at the beginning of January, it sets around two hours before sunrise, and by the end of the month, it sets about four hours before sunrise. In January 2025, Jupiter is positioned near the bright star Aldebaran and the Pleiades star cluster in the constellation Taurus. citeturn0search0

Additionally, Mars is becoming increasingly prominent in the night sky. It rises around 6:08 PM and remains visible throughout the night, reaching its opposition on January 16, 2025, when it will be at its brightest and visible all night. citeturn0search3

Given the time of your observation, it's most probable that the bright object in the eastern sky is Jupiter.

navlistUpcoming Celestial Events in January 2025turn0news12,turn0news13
Jupiter would make sense, it's huge, and very bright.

Exactly! Jupiter is often the brightest object in the night sky after the Moon, thanks to its massive size and reflective cloud layers. Its brilliance can make it quite a showstopper, especially when it's positioned prominently like it is now. If you have binoculars or a telescope, you might even spot some of its largest moons—Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto—or its iconic cloud bands!
